analysis: Both units are CHANGELOG.md base_text only (base lines 458-850). No patch, head text or hunk coordinates were supplied, so the actual PR change is not visible. This is a coverage limit, not evidence the change is safe, and I cannot say which lines the PR modified. The base text is historical release notes (v0.9.7 to v0.9.14 plus an unreleased section) and has no executable security behavior. It describes controls relevant to the canonical threat model: SSD prefix-cache defaults, a 30-minute TTL, account-scoped salts and HMAC lookup tags (T-041/SEC-035); App Attest authorization and key rotation (TB-011, T-052/T-053/T-054/T-057); MiMo memory admission; and a coordinator min-provider-version floor. Nothing in the visible text contradicts T-041. It repeats the 30-minute TTL, the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch and the per-donation demand gate. If the PR edits changelog claims about cache TTL, defaults or authorization, a later pass should check them against the source files (SSDPrefixCachePolicy, PrefixCachePolicy, App Attest services). No source changes were supplied that would affect an asset or trust boundary. No cross-file interactions can be assessed from these units.
